codeReview.summary: Successfully refactored MqttClient::publish_discovery() to use DiscoveryBuilder from launa-mqtt, eliminating duplicate hand-rolled JSON configs. All 20 entity configs now include origin, sw_version in device block, and entity_category on diagnostics/alert sensors. The discovery module was made no_std compatible by replacing serde_json::json! with alloc::format!-based JSON construction. All 82 launa-mqtt tests pass, and the ESP32 app compiles cleanly with no new warnings.

issues.description: Comment says 'Build and publish one entity at a time to avoid OOM on 32 KiB heap' but build_with_retain() actually creates ALL 20 DiscoveryMessage objects in a Vec simultaneously before iterating. The comment is misleading — it doesn't truly publish one-at-a-time. However, this is no worse than the old code (which also used alloc::vec![] to create all configs at once), and the Vec is dropped after the loop. For true one-at-a-time generation, DiscoveryBuilder would need an iterator-based API. This is a future improvement opportunity, not a regression.

The 'Last Fault' sensor does not have entity_category: 'diagnostic', though it is arguably a diagnostic-type entity. The validation contract (VAL-MQTT-004) only requires entity_category on 'Diagnostics and alert' sensors, so this is correct per spec. However, 'fault' is semantically a diagnostic sensor and could benefit from entity_category: 'diagnostic' in a future iteration.

sharedStateObservations.observation: The discovery module in launa-mqtt was converted from serde_json::json! to manual alloc::format!-based JSON construction to achieve no_std compatibility. This is a significant pattern worth noting — when workspace crates need to produce JSON in no_std, the convention is manual format! strings with helper functions (json_device_block, json_origin), not a JSON serialization library.
sharedStateObservations.evidence: crates/launa-mqtt/src/discovery.rs — json_device_block() and json_origin() helper functions using alloc::format!()

sharedStateObservations.observation: The DiscoveryBuilder no longer requires the 'std' feature — it was unconditionally exported by removing the #[cfg(feature = "std")] gates from both the mod declaration and the pub use statement in lib.rs. The serde/serde_json dependency is only needed for tests.
sharedStateObservations.evidence: crates/launa-mqtt/src/lib.rs — discovery module and DiscoveryBuilder/DiscoveryMessage exports are now unconditional

summary: PASS. The refactor correctly replaces hand-rolled discovery configs with DiscoveryBuilder, fixing the missing origin, sw_version, and entity_category fields. All 11 asserted validations (VAL-MQTT-001 through VAL-MQTT-009, VAL-MQTT-016, VAL-MQTT-017, VAL-MQTT-018) are addressed. The discovery module is now no_std compatible. Two non-blocking issues noted: (1) the 'one at a time' comment is misleading since all 20 configs are built simultaneously in a Vec, and (2) architecture.md is stale and still describes the old hand-rolled approach. Both are improvements for future work, not regressions.
